ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Consolidated List, New Zealand sanctions lists made under the Sanctions Act 2019, and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit's alerts; enhanced risk-based screening against OFAC's SDN list is required by most marine underwriting counterparties and is treated as a commercial/AML best-practice standard. PEPs and persons connected with PEPs must receive enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth/entity-purpose checks, and senior management approval before onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz), accessed via RealMe; name reservation and company incorporation are completed on the same electronic registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be in English and/or te reo Māori and may be indexed only in Latin script. The name must not be identical, nearly identical, or likely to be mistaken for an existing registered name or reserved name; ampersands, punctuation, and non-Latin characters are disregarded for distinguishability unless statutorily prescribed. All official registry entries are Romanized/transliterated; a transliteration certificate is required for non-English names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a name, the filing notice will identify the reason and original reference. Within 20 working days of rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Companies Office (via the Companies Office contact portal), attaching a legal submission on distinctiveness and any regulatory approval obtained; the Registrar will issue a final decision. A still-unsuccessful applicant may apply to the High Court for judicial review of the Registrar's decision; in practice, submitting a revised name or obtaining an approval from the relevant sector regulator (e.g., RBNZ for 'Insurance', FMA for 'Trust') is faster than litigation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A New Zealand registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand at which documents can be served during ordinary business hours; a purely virtual mailbox or PO Box is not compliant. For a marine claims surveyor, a professional registered-office service or co-working address with mail handling and service acceptance is acceptable for registry purposes, but the company must be able to demonstrate operational substance at the surveyor's actual place of business (the vessel terminal, office, or home office) if an AML/CFT supervisor or tax authority queries commercial reality.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated 8% probability of an unannounced inspection in the first 12 months, typically triggered only by a formal caution or an AML/CFT risk assessment; regular enforceable undertakings or site visits are more likely if the entity becomes a reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act or contracts with supervised insurance counterparties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cook Islands International Companies Act 1981-82, as amended (consolidated through the International Companies Amendment Act 2008-09), ss. 5-13 (incorporation procedure), ss. 14-24 (memorandum, articles, shares and charges), ss. 31-43 (directors, secretary, registered office and registered agent); New Zealand Companies Act 1993, Part 18 (ss. 330-345) (registration of overseas companies in New Zealand); Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 (NZ); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (NZ), Part 9A (financial advice licensing); Maritime Transport Act 1994 (NZ) and Maritime Rules Part 44 (marine surveyor accreditation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cook Islands: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA), Avarua, Rarotonga; New Zealand: Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington/Auckland, operating via the online Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Cook Islands: Form 1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company), supported by the Memorandum and Articles of Association and the registered agent's statutory declaration, culminating in the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of International Companies; New Zealand: Form 22 (Application for Registration of an Overseas Company) filed electronically with the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Cook Islands International Company; the Memorandum may declare an authorised capital of USD 1,000 divided into ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each (or no par value shares), and the subscriber may allot a single share for nominal consideration. No escrow account or bank deposit is required by the Cook Islands Registrar. For the New Zealand overseas company registration under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993, no minimum capital is prescribed for the branch; the applicant must merely disclose the issued share capital of the Cook Islands company in Form 22.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS IN WRITING OF THE SOLE SUBSCRIBER AND FIRST DIRECTOR OF [MARINE SURVEY CO CK IC] (the 'Company'), an International Company incorporated under the International Companies Act 1981-82 (Cook Islands), passed on the 5th day of July 2025 in accordance with Section 13 of the Act and Article 2.4 of the Articles of Association.

NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: That the authorised share capital of the Company be USD 1,000 divided into 1,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each, and that the subscriber's subscription of 100 ordinary shares at par be and is hereby accepted, allotted and fully paid in cash, and that the Secretary be and is hereby directed to enter the allotment in the register of members and to issue Share Certificate No. 1 accordingly.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE AND REGISTERED AGENT: That the registered office of the Company shall be situated in the Cook Islands at the office of [Registered Agent Name], an FSDA-licensed registered agent, at [street address, Avarua, Rarotonga], and that said registered agent is hereby appointed to hold the registered office, to maintain the register of members and the register of charges, and to accept service of process on behalf of the Company.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: That [Name] be and is hereby appointed as the first director of the Company to hold office until removal or replacement; that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as the Secretary of the Company; and that each such officer be and is hereby authorised to execute and deliver all documents necessary or advisable to effectuate the incorporation of the Company and its registration as an overseas company in New Zealand.

4. NEW ZEALAND BRANCH AND PROCESS AGENT: That the establishment of a branch in New Zealand under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993 be and is hereby approved; that the registered office of the branch in New Zealand be [NZ street address, Auckland]; and that [Name of NZ law firm] be and is hereby appointed as the New Zealand resident process agent for the service of documents on the Company in New Zealand.

5. POWER TO OPEN BANK ACCOUNTS AND OBTAIN LICENCES: That the opening of corporate bank accounts, including a New Zealand branch bank account, and the making of applications for the Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration, the Financial Advice Provider (FAP) licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, the Marine Surveyor Accreditation under the Maritime Transport Act 1994, and all requisite environmental, fire safety and occupational clearances be and is hereby authorised; and that the signature of any one of the Director or the Secretary, or the Branch Manager for the New Zealand account, shall be sufficient.

6. INDEMNITY: That the Company shall indemnify each officer and agent to the fullest extent permitted by the International Companies Act 1981-82.

CERTIFIED CORRECT, this 5th day of July 2025.

[Signature] _________________
Sole Director / Subscriber

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Reservation in the Cook Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cook Islands Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA), Rarotonga - online FSDA e-services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the FSDA electronic portal. The proposed name must end with 'Limited' or the suffix 'IC' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing name on the International Companies Register. Provide two alternative names in order of preference. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 60 days, during which the incorporation application must be filed.
required_dossiers: Completed FSDA name reservation application Form NC-01
Consent letter from the proposed FSDA-licensed registered agent
Certified copy of the subscriber's passport and proof of residential address
Details of any trademark or trade name registration relied upon in support of the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is declined or placed on hold for similarity, file a fresh application with alternative names within 10 business days; if the refusal is on grounds of confusing similarity, submit a written administrative review request to the FSDA Registry with trademark evidence and a legal memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting registered name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Registered Agent and Preparation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FSDA-licensed Registered Agent (private licensed corporate services provider) acting as intermediary before the Office of the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a written engagement letter with an FSDA-licensed registered agent. The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with the prescribed forms of the International Companies Act 1981-82, incorporating the authorised share capital, permitted objects (marine insurance claims inspection and survey services), and the agreement to assume a tax-exempt character. The subscriber signs the Memorandum; the agent submits the incorporation application to the Registrar and verifies the identity and source of funds of the beneficial owner pursuant to the AML/CFT regime.
required_dossiers: Signed engagement letter and corporate services agreement
Certified passport copy of the subscriber and any ultimate beneficial owner
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank reference letter for the subscriber
AML/CFT due diligence questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition on the constitutional documents, the registered agent will amend and re-file the Memorandum or Articles within 14 days; if the AML/CFT beneficial ownership declaration is queried, submit a supplementary declaration with corroborating identification documents and a notarised source-of-wealth statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Financial Services Development Authority, Rarotonga
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application (Form 1) together with the signed Memorandum and Articles of Association, the registered agent's statutory declaration confirming compliance with AML/CFT due diligence, and the consent of the proposed directors and secretary. Pay the government incorporation fee and the first annual registration fee via the FSDA payment portal. The Registrar acknowledges receipt and commences the statutory review.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Memorandum and Articles of Association (original signed copies)
Statutory declaration of the FSDA-licensed registered agent (AML/CFT compliance)
Consent forms of the proposed director and secretary
Receipt of payment of incorporation and annual fees
Name reservation certificate issued in Step 1
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for informality, the Registrar issues an inquiry notice and the registered agent has 14 days to file an amended application without re-payment of the incorporation fee; if rejected on AML/CFT grounds, file corrected beneficial ownership information and supporting bank references within 14 days; a further refusal may be appealed to the FSDA Appeals Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Adoption of Initial Corporate Governance Acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Services Development Authority, Rarotonga
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation. The subscriber then convenes the first board by written resolution: the board adopts the registered office, appoints officers, records the allotment of shares, approves the share certificate, and lodges the notices of appointment of director, secretary, and registered agent with the Registrar. The certificate and constitutional documents are then certified for use in the New Zealand registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (original)
Consent to act as director (Form)
Consent to act as secretary (Form)
Consent of the registered agent to hold the registered office
Notice of appointment of registered agent (Form 9)
Minutes or written resolutions of the first board meeting
Share certificate No. 1 and register of members extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a typographical or legal discrepancy, apply for a Certificate of Correction under the provisions of the International Companies Act; if a director or secretary consent is rejected, submit a fresh signed consent with a notarised signature within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of New Zealand Process Agent and Registered Office for the Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FSDA (Cook Islands) and New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) - in preparation for Part 18 registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Cook Islands company executes a power of attorney appointing a New Zealand resident process agent and adopts a New Zealand registered office address. The board approves the branch manager and the opening of a New Zealand branch operation. A certified English-language copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and the Constitutional Documents is prepared, with notarisation and apostille through the Cook Islands Ministry of Justice.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney appointing the New Zealand process agent (Form 24 under Part 18)
Registered office consent from the New Zealand service address provider
Lease agreement or service agreement for the New Zealand registered office
Certified copy of the Cook Islands Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association (English original)
Apostille certificates from the Cook Islands Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the New Zealand Companies Office requires further certification or translation of Cook Islands documents, obtain an apostille and, if requested, a certified English translation from an NZ-registered translator within 20 business days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Cook Islands International Company as an Overseas Company in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) - online via the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 22 (Application for Registration of an Overseas Company) electronically on the Companies Register. Provide the certified Certificate of Incorporation, the certified Memorandum and Articles of Association, the register of directors in New Zealand statutory format, and the power of attorney appointing the local agent for service of process. Pay the prescribed registration fee. The Registrar will register the company as an overseas company with a branch registration number, and the company may then lawfully carry on business in New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Form 22 (online application) with all prescribed annexures
Certified copy of the Cook Islands Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Register of directors and secretary in the New Zealand statutory format (including date and place of birth, residential address, and consent)
Power of attorney in favour of the New Zealand process agent
Consent of the New Zealand local agent for service of process
Notice of the New Zealand registered office address
Evidence of payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993, if the Registrar refuses registration for name conflict, the company may file a notice adopting a distinct 'New Zealand registered name' and re-submit Form 22; if the application is returned for deficient documents, cure the defect and re-submit within 30 days without re-payment of the fee; if the Registrar queries the process agent appointment, provide a fresh consent letter and substituted agent appointment within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Service Provider (FSP) Registration and Financial Advice Provider (FAP) Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) administered by the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the overseas company on the Financial Service Providers Register under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, selecting the service categories of 'financial advice' and 'insurance products'. Join an approved dispute resolution scheme (the Insurance and Financial Services Ombudsman or Financial Dispute Resolution Service). Prepare a compliance manual and, because marine insurance claims surveying may include providing regulated financial advice to policyholders, apply to the FMA for a Financial Advice Provider (FAP) licence under Part 9A of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, appointing a New Zealand resident Financial Advice Officer holding an NZ Certificate in Financial Advice (Level 5) or an equivalent qualification.
required_dossiers: FSPR online application (with NZBN or overseas company registration number, AML/CFT supervisor declaration, and business activity selection)
Dispute resolution scheme membership application and fee
FAP licence application to the FMA (Form FAP), including business plan, compliance manual, and risk management programme
Professional indemnity insurance certificate (minimum NZD 1,000,000)
Curriculum vitae and qualification certificates of the proposed Financial Advice Officer and nominated representatives
AML/CFT compliance regime documentation, including the appointment of the FMA as AML/CFT supervisor for the FSP
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA imposes additional licensing conditions or requires a more detailed remediation plan, submit a supplementary compliance addendum within 20 working days; if the dispute resolution scheme declines membership, select an alternative FMA-approved scheme within 10 business days; if the FSPR application is rejected for incomplete AML/CFT details, file corrected information and re-submit within 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Compliance, Tax Notifications and Licence Implantation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) New Zealand, Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Maritime New Zealand, and the NZ Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the IRD for a New Zealand IRD number and register for GST if annual taxable supplies will exceed NZD 60,000. Confirm the non-resident company branch status and file the IR596 (non-resident company registration). In the Cook Islands, obtain the automatic tax exemption certificate under the International Companies Act and file the annual return with the Registrar. In parallel, file the Maritime New Zealand Marine Surveyor Accreditation application under Maritime Rules Part 44 for the vessel hull and cargo claims inspection scope, together with the fire safety, building warrant of fitness and WorkSafe clearance applications for the branch premises.
required_dossiers: IRD non-resident company registration form (IR596)
GST registration application (IR322)
Cook Islands annual return and tax exemption application
Maritime New Zealand Marine Surveyor Accreditation application, including professional qualifications and insurance certificate
Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire safety certificate application
Building Act 2004 warrant of fitness application for the survey office and equipment store
WorkSafe New Zealand notification and health and safety risk assessment
Copy of the overseas company registration certificate and FSP/FAP licences
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD queries the permanent establishment status of the branch, submit the New Zealand-Cook Islands double tax agreement analysis and the Cook Islands tax residence certificate; if Maritime NZ challenges the surveyor's professional experience, provide a competency portfolio and arrange an oral assessment; if any license application is late, apply for late-filing penalty remission within 30 days and pay any assessed penalties to preserve the license.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime New Zealand (Maritime Safety Authority, Wellington) for marine surveyor accreditation under the Maritime Transport Act 1994 and Maritime Rules Part 44; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Financial Service Providers Register for marine insurance claims-advisory financial advice licensing under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 Part 9A; Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand and the relevant territorial authority for environmental and resource consent matters; WorkSafe New Zealand for occupational health and safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Surveyor Accreditation (Maritime New Zealand) for Vessel Hull and Cargo Damage Marine Claims Inspection Survey; Financial Advice Provider (FAP) Licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (where the surveyor provides regulated financial advice in relation to marine insurance claims); Overseas Company Registration and Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration as mandatory prerequisites.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) Te Mana Rauhī Taiao, New Zealand, in conjunction with the territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-Only / Permitted Activity category - no full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report is mandated for a non-industrial marine survey office and claims inspection facility; however, a resource consent (restricted discretionary) is required from the territorial authority if the premises include a workshop discharging trade wastewater, a marine access jetty, or storage of hazardous substances in quantities above the permitted thresholds under the RMA and the Health and Safety at Work (Hazardous Substances) Regulations 2017.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Resource Management Act 1991 permitted-activity discharge standards for any trade wastewater outlet: pH 6.0-9.0, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) not exceeding 30 mg/L, total suspended solids (TSS) not exceeding 50 mg/L, and no visible oil or grease sheen; VOC emissions from cleaning solvents and degreasing agents not to exceed 500 mg/m3 at the extraction point; hazardous wastes (used oils, batteries, ultrasonic testing chemicals, and electronic survey equipment) must be consigned to a WorkSafe-licensed hazardous waste contractor in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and the Environmental Protection Authority hazardous substances compliance certificates (annual HSNO location certification) for any storage exceeding 100 L or 100 kg aggregate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) fire safety certificate and annual building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004 (fire alarm, egress lighting, and suppression systems); structural load and seismic certification to NZS 1170.5 (Structural Design Actions - Earthquake) for the survey office, equipment store, and any inspection pier or launching facility; WorkSafe New Zealand occupational health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a workplace environment assessment, asbestos management plan for the premises, personal flotation device (PFD) and lifejacket compliance for marine boarding operations, and a documented safety management system for vessel boardings and high-risk hold inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, operating through the MyIR online portal and the IRD business.govt.nz services; customs and excise matters are administered by the New Zealand Customs Service with GST on imports collected at the border.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity engaging in a taxable activity in New Zealand must register for New Zealand GST and obtain an IRD number by filing the IR596 Application for IRD number for non-resident companies and the GST registration application (IR421) through the Inland Revenue Department. For non-resident companies without a physical New Zealand presence, registration may be completed via an approved tax agent or through the MyIR portal with certified entity documents, proof of foreign tax residency, and a New Zealand appointed agent where required. Companies incorporated in New Zealand receive an IRD number upon incorporation through the New Zealand Companies Office; for foreign-incorporated entities deriving New Zealand-sourced income or making supplies connected with New Zealand, a separate application to IRD is mandatory before commencing taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not maintain a check-the-box classification regime analogous to the United States; however, a non-resident company may be treated as tax resident under the New Zealand domestic rules if central management and control is exercised in New Zealand (with applicable double tax agreement tie-breakers) and may elect to become a wholly-owned group company for GST grouping purposes under Section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Hybrid mismatch rules under Subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 apply to structured arrangements, but there is no elective hybrid entity classification. For qualifying foreign superannuation schemes and certain foreign investment vehicles, specific elective rules may apply under the Income Tax Act 2007.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Registration is compulsory if the supplier makes taxable supplies in New Zealand exceeding NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, or if supplies in the next 12 months are expected to exceed NZD 60,000; non-resident suppliers must register for GST if they supply remote services to New Zealand resident consumers in excess of the threshold, and non-resident businesses are generally required to register for GST on all taxable supplies regardless of turnover when they are carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand, except for non-resident suppliers of low-value cross-border services who may use the simplified registration and return regime without a physical presence threshold of no more than NZD 60,000 in respect of those services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no government-mandated real-time e-invoicing clearance or continuous transaction controls for domestic B2B GST; the primary mandate is the requirement to issue a valid tax invoice (in paper or electronic form) within 28 days of a request, meeting prescribed content requirements under Section 24 of the GST Act, and to use the New Zealand Peppol network if supplying government entities that require e-invoicing. The Inland Revenue Department accepts standard e-invoicing formats and has no digital stamping or real-time fiscal API pre-clearance requirement; however, electronic records and invoices must be retained for seven years and be capable of being produced in a readable format on IRD demand. GST returns are filed electronically via MyIR.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of goods from New Zealand where the supplier has shipped the goods out of New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply (or the supplier holds evidence of the removal from New Zealand), including direct exports, goods exported as part of passenger baggage, and services supplied in relation to exported goods. Offshore supplies of services to non-residents are zero-rated where the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed and the services are not supplied in connection with land or moveable property in New Zealand, and not supplied to a person in New Zealand for a taxable activity. Additionally, certain services physically performed outside New Zealand and intellectual property rights supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated under Section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, subject to specific anti-avoidance rules. Marine insurance surveying services performed in respect of goods to be exported, or performed outside New Zealand, may qualify if the recipient is a non-resident and not in New Zealand at the time of supply and the services are not supplied in connection with taxable property in New Zealand; vessel hull and cargo surveyors should confirm they are not arranging or facilitating insurance as a separate taxable supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Entry (Export Declaration) and approved electronic clearance via Trade Single Window (Tradex)
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing actual removal of goods from New Zealand
Commercial invoice issued by the supplier to the overseas customer showing zero-rated supply
Certificate of insurance declaration / marine survey report and contract evidencing the supply to the non-resident recipient
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/PayPal/Wise statements evidencing receipt of foreign currency consideration for export sales
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Section 108 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, the Commissioner of Inland Revenue may adjust zero-rated treatment if the exporter fails to evidence actual exportation within the required timeframe, resulting in an assessment of GST at 15% plus use-of-money interest from the original due date. Knowingly or recklessly providing false or misleading information to claim zero-rating constitutes an offence under the Tax Administration Act 1994, with penalties up to NZD 10,000 for individuals and NZD 50,000 for companies for a first offence, and up to NZD 50,000 for individuals and NZD 100,000 for subsequent offences; in addition, an evasions shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall may apply. The IRD has a dedicated international and high-wealth audit programme and may exchange information under New Zealand's tax treaties and the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters; retrospective clawback of input credits and penalties of 20% or 40% for not taking reasonable care or taking an unacceptable tax position apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua; sole monetary, prudential and financial-system stability authority. There is no separate foreign exchange administration body; exchange controls were fully liberalised in 1984. The Overseas Investment Act 2005 applies only to sensitive land, fishing quota and material assets, not to ordinary FX conversion, corporate treasury operations or service-export proceeds of a marine insurance surveying company.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible under IMF Article VIII obligations. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted for resident and non-resident entities. A Tax-Exempt-Zone International Company may convert NZD or foreign currency without any RBNZ approval, and may repatriate dividends, interest, loan repayments, service fees and liquidation proceeds without an exchange-control licence. The only practical hurdles are fiscal and reporting in nature: non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at the treaty rate of 15% under the NZ–Cook Islands Double Taxation Agreement, thin-capitalisation limits on shareholder debt, CRS/AEOI disclosure of ultimate beneficial owners, and arm's-length transfer-pricing expectations of Inland Revenue. No balance-of-payments approval is required for profit remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender or conversion obligation on export proceeds. The Foreign Exchange Control Regulations were revoked by the Foreign Exchange Control (Revocation) Order 1984, and no timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts. A marine insurance surveyor providing vessel-hull and cargo-damage claims inspection services to overseas underwriters may lawfully hold export proceeds indefinitely in a foreign-currency account at a registered New Zealand bank or repatriate them to NZD via the normal interbank market. For statistical coding, the Surveyor should report the underlying service export to Statistics New Zealand if annual receipts exceed the institutional threshold (NZD 1 million), but no exchange-control permission is triggered.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and NZD Settlement Account
Operational Account and Segregated Claims-Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: CONDITIONAL-MEDIUM. Wise is the designated fintech corridor (target_payment_rails: Underwriter_Wire, Wise). Wise NZ operates as a registered Financial Service Provider under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and is licensed under the NZ/Australian e-money regime, safeguarding client funds with tier-1 custodian banks; however, Wise is not a registered bank under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and cannot provide capital escrow custody or regulated term lending. The legal constraint is that an International Company classified as Tax-Exempt-Zone with non-resident beneficial owners may be declined by Wise's proprietary risk engine if any controller is tax-resident in a FATF greylisted or monitored jurisdiction. Therefore, Wise is legally viable only for low-value operational remittances (maximum NZD 50,000 per transaction and cumulative NZD 250,000 per month); all primary treasury, premium pass-through and claims-settlement flows must be cleared through a locally incorporated registered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto in-person interview mandate applies. New Zealand's AML/CFT Act 2009 and the RBNZ Supervision Framework do not statutorily require face-to-face identification, but all tier-1 commercial banks maintain an internal policy requiring a physical meeting with the appointed director(s) and any signatory for a Tax-Exempt-Zone International Company with non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership. Remote onboarding is available only where the company has an existing one-year banking relationship with an equivalent regulated entity, the directors pass a recorded video-call verification, and the statutory NZ-resident director requirement under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993 is satisfied. In practice, the physical interview is mandatory for first-time corporate clients; after onboarding, all transactional banking can be executed digitally.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore International Company status without demonstrable New Zealand economic substance or payroll presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Certified certificate of incorporation; (ii) New Zealand Companies Office overseas-company registration certificate and registered-office address; (iii) Commercial Marine Surveyor statutory licence and, where claims-advisory services are provided, the New Zealand Financial Service Provider registration number (FSPR); (iv) executed lease agreement for physical NZ premises; (v) professional indemnity insurance certificate with minimum NZD 2 million coverage; (vi) written substance memorandum describing the surveyor's operational capacity, vessel-flag/IMO tracking procedures, and anticipated flow-of-funds statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners incorporated in or tax-resident in a higher-risk or monitored jurisdiction (e.g., Cook Islands shareholder of the International Company)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Complete trust deed and shareholding/control chart; (ii) source of wealth (SOW) and source of funds (SOF) statements dated within 90 days; (iii) tax-residence certificates for all ultimate beneficial owners; (iv) four-year relationship reference letter from an internationally recognised bank; (v) Politically Exposed Person (PEP) declarations; (vi) global-screening and negative-media report from a reputable sanctions/AML data provider, dated within 30 days of the KYC review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear funding chain behind inbound capital-injection wire transfers from affiliated or interposed treasury vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Board resolution approving the capital contribution; (ii) share-subscription agreement or promissory-note contract; (iii) originator bank statement evidencing payment only from the shareholder's corporate account with no cash, third-party, or custodial-wallet funding; (iv) AML questionnaire for the underlying funding structure; (v) explanation of any interposed Cook Islands International Company holding layers, including consolidated ownership schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine claims-disbursement pattern creating perception of an unlicensed insurance fund-flow or premium collection without an insurance licence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Signed engagement contract with the appointing underwriter or adjusting house; (ii) executed marine survey report and fee invoice; (iii) segregated claims-escrow account agreement demonstrating that the Surveyor acts as a disbursing agent on behalf of principals and never commingles third-party claim funds with operating revenue; (iv) written confirmation from a New Zealand financial-services lawyer that the activity falls outside the licensing scope of the Insurance (Prudential Supervision) Act 2010; (v) quarterly compliance certificate to the bank's regulatory team.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the NZ settlement account are executed through a SWIFT MT103 payment initiated from the shareholder's corporate bank to the beneficiary tier-1 bank's BIC. New Zealand operates a purpose-code-free FX regime; however, the originator must embed ISO 20022/TSF remittance information reading 'Capital injection – share subscription' and the New Zealand Companies Office registration number. The beneficiary bank performs inbound AML and sanctions screening; funds are credited T+0 in NZD via the settlement-account relationship, with real-time availability through the ESAS clearing system. Supporting documentation for the bank's regulatory pack: board resolution, share-allotment form, certificate of compliance, and a signed statement confirming no cash or unregulated-electronic-money rails were used. There is no RBNZ limit on inbound non-resident capital for a marine survey service company, but inflows exceeding NZD 10 million require balance-of-payments statistical coding and may trigger Overseas Investment Act screening if any asset acquired is 'sensitive'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound professional-fee remittances and claims pass-through settlements are cleared over SWIFT MT103 with Global Payments Innovation (gpi) tracking, using the NZ registered bank's correspondent network (USD via CHIPS/Fedwire, GBP via CHAPS, EUR via TARGET2). For underwriters requiring documentary security, a commercial letter of credit (UCP600) may be issued by an NZ registered bank on presentation of the signed survey contract, survey report and commercial invoice; the beneficiary's confirming bank then negotiates against conforming documents. Domestic NZD payments to local insurers or agents settle through the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) in real time. Foreign-currency outflows are netted through Nostro accounts with end-of-day reconciliation. Wise is authorised only as a secondary rail for low-value claim refunds or small fee reimbursements up to NZD 15,000 per transaction, never for capital escrow or premium aggregates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Direct spot and forward FX contracts (maturity up to 24 months) executed with an NZ registered dealing bank, supported by a standard ISDA/ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Option Master Agreement
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) permitted for illiquid emerging-market currencies where the marine surveyor's claims-settlement book accumulates exotic-currency exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) on intercompany shareholder debt, subject to thin-capitalisation documentation
Vanilla FX options (purchased puts and calls) used exclusively for downside protection; no writing of uncovered options, no leverage beyond the notional operating requirement
Short-dated FX swaps (up to 3 months) for liquidity smoothing between the operational account and the claims-escrow account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (NZBN Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one calendar month after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cumulative late-filing fine of NZD 50 per month for directors (maximum NZD 500); failure to file for two months triggers a default reminder and after six months the Registrar may strike the company off the Register; re-instatement subsequently requires court proceedings (NZD 153.58) or Registrar discretion (NZD 76.79) plus all arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: FSP Annual Confirmation (Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) – Financial Service Providers Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the anniversary of the date the company is first registered as a financial service provider
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic removal from the FSP Register upon non-confirmation; providing marine insurance surveying services as a regulated financial service while unregistered constitutes an offence carrying fines up to NZD 300,000 for a company and NZD 10,000 per day while the contravention continues.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income Tax Return (IR4) – nil/defective return for tax-exempt offshore companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date: due by 7 July of the following income year; for a non-standard balance date: due by the 28th day of the fourth month after the balance date. A tax-exempt offshore company is required to file only if so required by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NZD 250, increasing to NZD 500 if the return is not filed by the one-month extension deadline; late-payment interest at the underpaid tax rate (8.9% per annum) accrues from the day after the due date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax (GST) Return (GST101) – only if taxable activity exceeds NZD 60,000 turnover
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For GST-registered marine survey suppliers: one-monthly return and payment due on the 28th of the following month where prior-twelve-month turnover exceeded NZD 24 million; otherwise two-monthly returns are due on the 28th of the month after the end of the taxable period (e.g., Jan–Feb period due 28 March).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NZD 50 per day up to NZD 250 per return; late-payment interest at 8.9% per annum (rising to 9.8% per annum from April 2025).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company is a large entity (aggregate total assets exceeding NZD 60 million or total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million for each of two consecutive accounting periods) or is otherwise a reporting entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; a shareholder holding 5% or more of the shares may independently trigger a compulsory audit. A small marine insurance surveying company that does not reach these thresholds is not required to file audited financial statements unless the Constitution or a shareholder notice requires it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB) for large and reporting entities; simplified 'Simple Format Reporting' (New Zealand small‑entity accounting standards) may be used for non-reporting small companies below the asset/revenue thresholds.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not impose a separate annual beneficial-ownership declaration filing for private companies; however, the company must keep an up‑to‑date share register, record every transfer in the Register of Members, file a notice of share allotment/transfer with the Companies Office, and confirm the current member/director record at each annual return anniversary. A board minute documenting the UBO confirmation and the identity of every new or departing ultimate beneficial owner is required at year‑end.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – 1,500 per annum (NZD 600 – 2,500, exclusive of disbursements)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 8,000 (NZD 4,000 – 14,000) for a small‑to‑medium marine survey undertaking when an audit is voluntarily or constitutionally required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Preferential treatment includes: R&D tax credit of 15% of qualifying R&D expenditure; immediate deduction for low-value assets (threshold NZD 5,000); 20% depreciation loading for certain plant and equipment. A non-resident international marine insurance surveying company with no New Zealand-source income may have nil effective NZ tax liability, but the statutory headline rate remains 28%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or via approved tax intermediaries/software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Provisional tax instalments are generally due three times a year (7th day of the fourth, eighth, and twelfth months after balance date) based on prior year residual income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 and final payment are due by 7 July following the income year. For non-standard balance dates, the return is due by the 7th day of the fourth month after the balance date. Registered tax agents can extend these deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-source income. Marine surveying fees are NZ-source to the extent services are physically performed in NZ.
Deduct expenses directly attributable to the NZ-source income; overheads should be apportioned on a just and reasonable basis.
Calculate as Box 1 minus Box 2. A loss may be carried forward indefinitely, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test.
Enter losses brought forward from prior years that satisfy the continuation of shareholder ownership test. Maintain records of continuity.
Net amount after applying allowable losses. If nil, the return must be filed with nil taxable income.
Compute tax on taxable income at the corporate rate. No reduced rate for non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits, RWT, and other credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim imputation credits attached to NZ dividends received and foreign tax credits. Non-residents must attach supporting certificate(s) to claim treaty relief.
Settle any outstanding amount. Ensure any dividend or royalty payments are subject to NRWT before remittance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 per return. Late payment penalty of 1% per month on the unpaid tax, plus a further 4% after six months. Use-of-money interest (currently 8.76% for underpayments) accrues daily. Shortfall penalties can rise to 150% of the tax avoidance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on non-imputed dividends; 15% NRWT on fully imputed dividends. Treaty rates typically reduce portfolio dividends to 15% and substantial shareholding dividends (10% or more) to 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide the NZ payer with a completed Tax Residence Certificate (IR 290) and a valid declaration of non-resident status before the dividends are paid. The payer must withhold at the reduced treaty rate only after receiving this documentation and retain it for audit. For residency certificates, the beneficiary must apply to its own tax authority; the certificate is then accepted by IRD if it confirms treaty residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; however, an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply if certain conditions are met, effectively replacing NRWT. Royalties: statutory NRWT 15%. Under most NZ DTAs, interest is reduced to 10% and royalties to 10%, subject to beneficial ownership and TRC requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory monetary threshold for maintaining a Local File or Master File. However, the IRD Transfer Pricing Guidelines expect contemporaneous documentation for cross-border related-party transactions with an aggregate annual value exceeding NZD 3 million. For Country-by-Country reporting, a multinational group with consolidated revenue of NZD 1.14 billion or more must file a CbC report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as seen in the GCC, but the general anti-avoidance rule (BG1 ITA 2007) invalidates arrangements lacking commercial substance. For a marine insurance surveying company, maintaining physical presence, qualified staff, and board control in NZ is essential to support tax residency or non-residency claims. Inland Revenue may also apply the delegated profit attribution rules to foreign-owned entities that lack substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting NZ-source survey income or fabricating expenses on the IR4 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994, s 143B – fine up to NZD 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civil shortfall penalty up to 150% of the tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false declarations or direct the evasion are personally liable for civil penalties and may face imprisonment; travel bans and disallowance under the Companies Act 1993 can also be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mispricing cross-border charges to related parties (e.g., inflated administration fees paid to an offshore parent) without contemporaneous arm's length documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRD may adjust the taxable income and impose a shortfall penalty of 20% or 40% depending on whether the taxpayer failed to take reasonable care or used an unacceptable interpretation. Re-computation may trigger additional NRWT on deemed dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who were party to the arrangement may be jointly and severally liable when they authorised the incorrect pricing and failed to ensure proper records; legal professional privilege is not available in tax fraud cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and File Dividend/Interest/Royalty Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting profits to shareholders abroad without deducting NRWT, or failing to file the relevant NRWT return (IR 67) on time.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NRWT under-assessment plus use-of-money interest and late payment penalties (1% per month). A punitive shortfall penalty of 100% of the unpaid NRWT may be applied for total absence of reasonable care.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable to the amount of the unremitted NRWT if the company cannot pay and the failure was knowingly allowed (Tax Administration Act 1994, s 136B). Overdue taxes may lead to a travel ban and statutory civil debt remedies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating from a post-office box with no physical office, staff, or board decisions in New Zealand while claiming non-resident status or sourcing income offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may disregard the arrangement via the general anti-avoidance rule, re-assessing all income as NZ-source and imposing shortfall penalties (up to 150%). The company may also be struck off the Companies Register, resulting in the loss of the marine insurance surveying statutory licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit the company to trade without genuine substance may be liable for wrongful trading under the Companies Act 1993 (s 135); where the company is used as a façade to evade tax, courts may pierce the corporate veil, making directors personally liable for the full tax debt and subject to comparison orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing marine claims inspection and loss adjusting services without holding the required statutory licence, or failing to perform customer due diligence when accepting underwriter wire transfers (e.g., from an overseas reinsurer).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed operation under the Insurance (Prudential Supervision) Act 2010 attracts a fine of up to NZD 1 million and an injunction to cease trading. Breach of the AML/CFT Act 2009 may result in fines up to NZD 2 million for an individual and NZD 5 million for a company; continual non-compliance can also result in criminal conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly consent or connive in the breach face personal criminal liability under the AML/CFT Act; the court may also impose a management ban of up to 10 years. Travel bans may be issued to prevent forum flight.
